title: Showing the way is Allah's own task.
subtitle: Guidance is His responsibility, walking it is yours
then: Qatadah said this means {idea}We will explain what is lawful and what is prohibited{/idea}. Others said whoever walks the path of guidance reaches Allah. Ibn Kathir compares it to: {idea}upon Allah is to explain the straight path{/idea}.
now: You feel lost about a big decision: a job offer, a move, a relationship. {reward}The road is not hidden from you.{/reward} Allah has promised to show it. Your part is to ask and to look.
old: I have to figure out what is right all by myself.
new: Allah has taken it on Himself to show the way; I only need to seek it.
try: Bring one decision you are stuck on to Allah in a short dua today.

title: This life and the next both belong to Allah.
subtitle: Full control of the first and the last
then: Ibn Kathir explains it as Allah saying: {idea}they both belong to Us and I am in complete control of them{/idea}. The stingy man of the first half thought he owned his world. {trap}He did not own either one.{/trap}
now: You chase a promotion as if your manager owns your future, and leave the Hereafter for later. {idea}Both are in the same Hand.{/idea} You can ask the One who owns both.
old: This world is up to me; the next one is up to Allah.
new: Both this life and the next are in Allah's control, so I ask Him for both.
try: Ask Allah today for one good thing in this world and one in the next.

title: A clear warning about a blazing Fire.
subtitle: A warning given out of care
then: Mujahid said the word means {trap}blazing{/trap}. An-Nu'man bin Bashir reported the Prophet ﷺ saying in a sermon, {idea}I have warned you of the Fire{/idea}, so loudly that someone in the marketplace could hear it.
now: A doctor tells you plainly that your blood pressure is dangerous. It is not cruelty, it is the most caring thing she can say. {reward}A warning given in time is a gift.{/reward}
old: Warnings about the Fire are just meant to frighten me.
new: Being warned clearly means I am being given a chance.
try: Think of one habit you know is harming you, and take one step away from it today.

title: Only the most wretched will enter it.
subtitle: The Fire is for those who refuse
then: Ibn Kathir says none will enter it {trap}surrounded on all sides{/trap} except the most wretched. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}all of my followers will enter Paradise except whoever refuses{/reward}. Asked who refuses, he said whoever disobeys him.
now: You worry you are not good enough for Allah's mercy. The door is open wide. {reward}The hadith says the only ones left out are the ones who refuse.{/reward} {idea}You are reading this. You have not refused.{/idea}
old: Paradise is for a few perfect people.
new: The door is wide open; only the one who refuses stays out.
try: Do one act of obedience today with the thought that you are saying yes.

title: He denied in his heart and turned away in deeds.
subtitle: Two parts of refusal
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}denied, meaning in his heart{/trap}. {trap}Turned away, meaning from acting with his limbs{/trap} and doing deeds properly. The wretched one does both.
now: You tell yourself your heart is good, so the prayers and the kindness can wait. {idea}The verse treats the heart and the hands as a pair.{/idea} Turning away with the hands is half of the problem.
old: My intentions are good, so the actions do not matter as much.
new: What I believe and what I do both count; neither replaces the other.
try: Turn one good intention you have held for a while into an action today.

title: The most mindful will be kept far from it.
subtitle: The one who is saved from the Fire
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}the righteous, pure, most pious person will be saved from the Fire{/reward}. The surah now describes him in detail, as it did the wretched one. {idea}Two people, two ends.{/idea}
now: You picture safety as a locked door or an insurance policy. {reward}This verse gives a different picture: a person kept far from harm because of who they became.{/reward}
old: Being safe is about what I own or who I know.
new: Real safety is being someone Allah keeps far from the Fire.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to keep you far from the Fire.

title: He gives his wealth to make himself clean.
subtitle: Giving as a way of purifying the self
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}he spends his wealth in obedience of his Lord in order to purify himself{/reward}, his wealth, and what Allah gave him. Many scholars said these verses were revealed about {idea}Abu Bakr As-Siddiq{/idea}, though the wording is general.
now: You give to the food bank and feel lighter walking out. That is not a coincidence. {reward}The giving cleaned something in you.{/reward} The bag of groceries helped two people.
old: Charity is something I do for other people.
new: When I give, I am also cleaning my own soul.
try: Give something today and notice how it changes your mood afterwards.

title: He is not paying anyone back for a favour.
subtitle: Giving that is not a trade
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}his giving is not done to gain some favour in return{/idea}. He tells how Urwah bin Mas'ud said he owed Abu Bakr a debt, and {reward}Abu Bakr was angered at being thought owed anything{/reward}.
now: You help a coworker move flat and later feel annoyed they never offered help back. {trap}Without noticing, the help became a loan.{/trap} {reward}Giving with no invoice is a different thing.{/reward}
old: If I do something nice, I expect something back.
new: My best giving has no bill attached to it.
try: Do one favour today for someone who cannot repay you.

title: He gives only to seek his Lord's Face.
subtitle: The one goal behind his giving
then: Ibn Kathir says he gives {reward}hoping to attain the blessing of seeing Him in the Gardens of Paradise{/reward}. Nothing less is the goal. {idea}Not thanks, not status, not a return.{/idea}
now: You post about a fundraiser and keep checking who liked it. {trap}The likes start to feel like the point.{/trap} {reward}This verse points past every screen to one Face.{/reward}
old: It is fine if some of my giving is for how it looks.
new: The highest giving looks only toward Allah's Face.
try: Give one thing today that no one will ever know about.

title: And he will be content.
subtitle: The promise that ends the surah

key.label: What he gave up, what he got

then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}those with these characteristics will be pleased{/reward}. He mentions the Prophet ﷺ hoping that Abu Bakr would be {reward}called from every gate of Paradise{/reward}.
now: You gave quietly and nobody thanked you. Maybe it still stings a little. {reward}The surah ends by telling you that you will be satisfied.{/reward} Not a little, not partly. Pleased.
old: If no one thanks me, my giving was wasted.
new: Allah promises the quiet giver that he will be fully content.
try: Recall one unthanked kindness you did. Leave it with Allah and let it go.
